Everyone debating the AI race is arguing about chips and software.

The real bottleneck is electricity.

Berkeley Lab says data centers could take 9.5% to 15.3% of all US power demand by 2030. Whoever can reliably generate it wins.

Missouri can.

embedded_ivos.text: I hear a lot from my neighbors on Medicare who are worried about unchecked technology and AI impacting their ability to access care. china_race_dynamics.text:

Why? Because they want to win the AI race. 

Don't do Beijing's work for them. Build here. Win here. https://t.co/tpx88TFSyY

china_race_dynamics.text:

New report: a China-linked network helped block or delay $23.6B in US data center projects. This is real. Ask if what you read online is Chinese propaganda.

https://t.co/hEzJgxxcXM https://t.co/gGpcRn6cyH

china_race_dynamics.text: The question is, are we going to be in control of this or are we going to let China take control or another country dominate the United States? It's extremely important that we are the nation that has the data centers that house these AI servers.

china_race_dynamics.text: It's extremely important that we own the code, that we don't end up in a situation like we did with TikTok, for example, where China has access to the data and they control the code. So this is why the United States needs to be a leader in artificial intelligence.
